diffs.headline: OBBBA tax law enables immediate domestic R&D and capex expensing
diffs.summary: Meta added disclosure on the July 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which allows immediate expensing of domestic R&D and certain capex starting in 2025. The provisions reduce U.S. federal cash tax payments for 2025 and future years, subject to the 15% Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: On July 4, 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) was enacted, introducing several significant U.S. income tax provisions that reduced our U.S. federal cash tax payments for the remainder of 2025 and future years.
diffs.signalNote: Immediate R&D and capex expensing meaningfully boosts near-term free cash flow conversion during Meta's heavy AI infrastructure buildout.

diffs.headline: AI roadmap uncertainty and product shifts highlighted as key risks
diffs.summary: Meta expanded its AI risk disclosures, noting that market acceptance of AI features is uncertain and that it regularly makes significant changes to AI product roadmaps as technological and market understanding evolves.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: We regularly evaluate our product roadmaps and make significant changes as our understanding of the technological challenges and market landscape of AI, as well as our product ideas and designs, continue to evolve.
diffs.signalNote: Frequent AI roadmap pivots underscore execution risk on multi-billion-dollar AI investments.

diffs.headline: Optimus humanoid robot commercialization added as formal risk factor
diffs.summary: Tesla introduced a dedicated risk factor for its Bots program, including Optimus, noting that development requires significant cash investments and management resources with no guarantee of commercialization or demand.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: We currently are developing Bots, including Optimus, and intend for these products, as well as accompanying services, to be an important part of our business going forward. While this development requires significant cash
diffs.signalNote: Formalizing Optimus as a standalone risk signals rising capital commitment to robotics ahead of commercial proof.

diffs.headline: Resale value guarantees added on bank-partnered vehicle leases
diffs.summary: Tesla disclosed that it originates leases and immediately transfers them to commercial banking partners under ASC 606 sale accounting, while providing capped resale value guarantees.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: We offer resale value guarantees to our commercial banking partners in connection with certain vehicle leasing programs. Under these programs, we originate the lease with our end customer and immediately transfer the lease
diffs.signalNote: Capped resale guarantees support upfront revenue recognition but create contingent residual-value exposure if used EV prices fall.

diffs.headline: Pharmaceutical tariff exemptions flagged as potentially temporary
diffs.summary: Eli Lilly added MD&A disclosure warning that while pharmaceuticals are currently exempt from certain newly imposed or paused U.S. and foreign tariffs, those exemptions may be terminated or excluded from future tariff actions.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: While pharmaceuticals are exempt from certain of these tariffs, such exemptions may be terminated or may not apply to any future tariffs. The precise impact of tariffs, trade protection measures, and other restrictions
diffs.signalNote: Loss of pharma tariff exemptions could pressure gross margins and complicate global API and manufacturing expansion.

diffs.headline: U.S.-China trade tensions cited as threat to market access and deals
diffs.summary: Lilly highlighted escalating U.S.-China tariffs, sanctions, and trade restrictions as risks that could increase scrutiny on market access, operations, and business development transactions.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: tensions between the U.S. and China, which have already led to a series of tariffs and sanctions, as well as other business restrictions, could further escalate based on additional trade restrictions, retaliation thereto
diffs.signalNote: Cross-border licensing and China commercial growth face heightened geopolitical friction.

diffs.headline: Tariffs, trade barriers, and consumer credit pressures added to risks
diffs.summary: Walmart added explicit risk language covering export and import restrictions, tariffs, trade barriers, higher consumer debt levels, and changes in consumer spending patterns.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: consumer credit, higher consumer debt levels, changes in consumer spending and shopping patterns, fluctuations in currency exchange rates, higher tax rates, imposition of new taxes or other changes in tax laws
diffs.signalNote: Import tariff exposure and stretched lower-income consumer credit remain key watchpoints for retail gross margins.

diffs.headline: AI, fintech, and cybersecurity talent retention and succession flagged
diffs.summary: Visa added risk disclosures emphasizing intense competition for specialized talent in fintech, AI, and cybersecurity, alongside risks around management succession planning and talent program scrutiny.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The market for highly skilled workers and leaders in our industry, especially in fintech, technology, AI, cybersecurity and other specialized areas, is extremely competitive.
diffs.signalNote: Rising competition for AI and cybersecurity talent could push operating expenses higher as Visa defends its network moat.

diffs.headline: Cash and marketable securities stand at $13.75B as of FY26 year-end
diffs.summary: Visa reported $12.9 billion in cash and cash equivalents plus $850 million in available-for-sale U.S. debt securities as of September 30, 2026.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: As of September 30, 2026, our cash and cash equivalents balance was $12.9 billion and primarily consisted of cash and money market funds. As of September 30, 2026, our available-for-sale debt securities balance was $850M
diffs.signalNote: Substantial balance sheet liquidity supports ongoing buybacks and strategic network investments.

diffs.headline: Talc reserve reversal of $7.0B offsets $0.8B Auris litigation charge
diffs.summary: Johnson & Johnson disclosed a $7.0 billion reversal of previously accrued talc reserves in 2025, alongside a $0.8 billion expense for Auris shareholder litigation and approximately $1.1 billion in opioid settlement payments.
diffs.priorExcerpt: (1) The fiscal years 2024 and 2023 include charges primarily for talc matters (See Note 19 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for more details).
diffs.currentExcerpt: (1) The fiscal year 2025 includes the reversal of approximately $7.0 billion, a significant portion of the previously accrued talc reserve and an expense of $0.8 billion for the Auris shareholder litigation.
diffs.signalNote: The $7.0B talc reserve release materially alters JNJ's legal liability overhang, though Auris and opioid payouts remain notable.

diffs.headline: Total debt jumps to $47.9B to fund $14.5B Intra-Cellular acquisition
diffs.summary: Total borrowings rose from $36.6 billion in 2024 to $47.9 billion at year-end 2025, driven by $9.2 billion in senior unsecured notes issued to help fund the $14.5 billion Intra-Cellular Therapies acquisition.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $24.5 billion at the end of 2024, and averaged $23.7 billion
diffs.currentExcerpt: Total borrowings at the end of 2025 and 2024 were $47.9 billion and $36.6 billion, respectively. The increase in the borrowings was primarily due to the issuance of new debt in the fiscal first quarter of 2025.
diffs.signalNote: Higher leverage from the Intra-Cellular deal shifts JNJ's capital structure and increases interest expense sensitivity.

diffs.headline: Mastercard Threat Intelligence launched with Recorded Future
diffs.summary: Mastercard highlighted the 2025 launch of Mastercard Threat Intelligence, integrating Recorded Future's cyber threat capabilities with its payment network to proactively detect cyberattacks and prevent fraud.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: In 2025, we launched Mastercard Threat Intelligence, which combines Mastercard's payment expertise and global network visibility with Recorded Future's leading cyber threat intelligence capabilities
diffs.signalNote: Value-added cybersecurity services deepen merchant and issuer stickiness beyond core payment rails.

diffs.headline: Total debt rises to $19.0B with next $750M maturity in November 2026
diffs.summary: Mastercard repaid $750 million of 2019 USD Notes in March 2025 and ended 2025 with $19.0 billion in total debt, up from $18.2 billion a year earlier, with the next $750 million maturity in November 2026.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Our total debt outstanding was $18.2 billion at December 31, 2024, with the earliest maturity of $750 million of principal occurring in March 2025.
diffs.currentExcerpt: In March 2025, $750 million of principal related to the 2019 USD Notes matured and was paid. Our total debt outstanding at December 31, 2025 was $19.0 billion, with the earliest maturity of $750 million
diffs.signalNote: Debt maturity profile remains well-laddered with manageable near-term refinancing needs.

diffs.headline: AbbVie pledges $100B in U.S. R&D and capex under federal pricing deal
diffs.summary: Subsequent to year-end 2025, AbbVie announced a voluntary agreement with the U.S. government to offer lower Medicaid prices, expand direct-to-patient offerings, and invest $100 billion in U.S. R&D and manufacturing over the next decade.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Subsequent to December 31, 2025, AbbVie announced a voluntary agreement with the U.S. government to further advance access and affordability of AbbVie's products in the U.S.
diffs.signalNote: The $100B 10-year U.S. investment pledge and Medicaid price concessions trade margin for policy certainty.

diffs.headline: Most-favored-nation drug pricing and tariffs flagged as margin risks
diffs.summary: AbbVie added risk disclosures warning that governments may pursue international reference pricing or most-favored-nation frameworks beyond the IRA, and that import/export tariffs could raise API and manufacturing costs.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: governments and other payers may pursue or implement additional approaches intended to reduce pharmaceutical costs, including arrangements or frameworks that reference international prices, most-favored-nation (MFN)
diffs.signalNote: MFN pricing proposals and API tariff exposure represent ongoing structural headwinds for pharma margins.

diffs.headline: Cash Capex metric formalized net of noncontrolling interest inflows
diffs.summary: Exxon Mobil added a formal definition of Cash Capital Expenditures (Cash Capex) in MD&A, netting inflows from noncontrolling interests for major projects against PP&E additions and investing outflows.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Cash capital expenditures (Cash Capex) are the sum of additions to property, plant, and equipment; additional investments and advances; and other investing activities including collection of advances; reduced by inflows
diffs.signalNote: Clarifying Cash Capex aligns Exxon's capital intensity reporting with major-project partner funding.

diffs.headline: Pegasus-1 offshore Cyprus gas discovery advances to evaluation
diffs.summary: Exxon disclosed that the Pegasus-1 exploratory well offshore Cyprus encountered a gas-bearing reservoir, with evaluations underway for potential commercialization.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The Pegasus-1 exploratory well was drilled offshore Cyprus and encountered a gas-bearing reservoir. Evaluations are ongoing to develop potential commercialization options.
diffs.signalNote: Cyprus gas discovery adds optionality to Exxon's Eastern Mediterranean LNG and upstream pipeline.

diffs.headline: Packaging and ingredient substance restrictions flagged as rising risk
diffs.summary: Coca-Cola added disclosure warning that existing or more restrictive regulations on substances in its products, packaging, and manufacturing processes could be proposed or enacted.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: substances present in certain of our products and/or their packaging, as well as processes used to make them, and it is possible that similar or more restrictive requirements may be proposed or enacted in the future.
diffs.signalNote: Tightening chemical and packaging rules could require reformulation or higher-cost sustainable packaging inputs.

diffs.headline: AI adoption added as formal business, compliance, and reputational risk
diffs.summary: Chevron added a new risk factor addressing its increasing use of AI in operations and information systems, citing risks from biased or incorrect outputs, compliance, and reputational harm.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Chevron is incorporating artificial intelligence technologies into its processes and these technologies may present business, compliance, and reputational risks
diffs.signalNote: Formal AI risk disclosure reflects deeper operational integration across upstream and downstream workflows.

diffs.headline: Tengizchevroil DD&A and CPChem margins weigh on equity affiliate income
diffs.summary: Chevron disclosed that 2025 equity affiliate income declined due to higher DD&A and lower realizations at Tengizchevroil (TCO) in Kazakhstan and weaker chemicals margins at CPChem, partially offset by GS Caltex.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Income from equity affiliates decreased in 2025 mainly due to lower upstream-related earnings from Tengizchevroil LLP (TCO) in Kazakhstan as higher liftings from the FGP project were more than offset by higher DD&A
diffs.signalNote: Higher FGP volumes at TCO are not yet offsetting elevated depreciation and softer chemical margins.

diffs.headline: Supreme Court IEEPA ruling enables $200M tariff recovery, $100M booked
diffs.summary: Procter & Gamble disclosed that following the February 2026 U.S. Supreme Court ruling invalidating IEEPA tariffs, it recognized recovery of half of the approximately $200 million in previously paid tariffs during Q4 FY26.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) were invalid. The Company previously paid approximately $200 million in IEEPA tariffs
diffs.signalNote: The $200M tariff recovery provides a direct one-time earnings and cash flow tailwind, with half still to be recognized.

diffs.headline: Adversarial AI phishing, deepfakes, and Middle East conflict added
diffs.summary: P&G expanded its cybersecurity risk factor to include adversarial AI phishing, deepfakes, and supply chain software compromises, while adding Middle East conflict risks to energy and supply chain costs.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Our IT/OT databases and systems and our third-party providers' databases and systems have been, and will likely continue to be, subject to advanced computer viruses or other malicious codes
diffs.currentExcerpt: phishing (including the use of adversarial AI techniques), social engineering, credential stuffing, automated vulnerability discovery, data encryption or exfiltration, deep fakes, hacking, supply chain software compromise
diffs.signalNote: Expanded cyber and geopolitical disclosures reflect heightened operational vigilance across global supply chains.

diffs.headline: Cisco Silicon One and Nexus One positioned as core AI data center stack
diffs.summary: Cisco updated its data center switching disclosures to emphasize Cisco Silicon One integration and its Nexus One unified on-premises and cloud-managed strategy for AI workloads.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Our data center switching offerings, led by the Nexus 9000 series, provide the foundation for mission critical data centers with high availability, scalability, and security
diffs.currentExcerpt: Central to this portfolio is the integration of Cisco Silicon One architecture, establishing a unified silicon foundation that delivers high performance and energy efficiency. Under our Nexus One strategy
diffs.signalNote: Unified silicon and full-stack AI networking position Cisco to capture hyperscale and enterprise AI infrastructure spend.

diffs.headline: Tariff and trade policy exposure flagged as potentially significant
diffs.summary: Cisco added MD&A language warning that exposure to new and proposed tariffs and trade policies is uncertain and could be significant if unmitigated.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Additionally, while we are exposed to new and proposed tariffs and other trade policies, the extent of such exposure is uncertain but could be significant if the exposure remains and we are unable to mitigate it.
diffs.signalNote: Hardware supply chain exposure leaves Cisco vulnerable to tariff-driven gross margin pressure.

diffs.headline: Competitor bundling and zero-margin pricing flagged as competitive threat
diffs.summary: Palantir added risk language warning that larger competitors may bundle functionality into existing products or sell at zero or negative margins to discourage customers from adopting Palantir platforms.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: larger competitors have substantially broader and more diverse product and service offerings and may be able to leverage their relationships with distribution partners and customers... including by selling at zero or negative
diffs.signalNote: Hyperscaler and incumbent software bundling could lengthen enterprise sales cycles and pressure pricing power.

diffs.headline: Aging store base requires ongoing capex and space reallocation
diffs.summary: Home Depot disclosed that its aging store base requires continual maintenance, capital investment, and space reallocation initiatives to support its interconnected shopping experience.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: We have an aging store base that requires maintenance, investment, and space reallocation initiatives to deliver the shopping experience that our customers desire.
diffs.signalNote: Sustained store reinvestment needs may limit near-term capex flexibility as Pro and digital initiatives scale.

diffs.headline: China Gardasil shipments remain paused with no resumption timeline
diffs.summary: Merck disclosed that it paused Gardasil and Gardasil 9 shipments to China in February 2025 due to elevated partner inventory and has not resumed shipments, with no predictable timeline for recovery.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Due to above normal inventory levels at the Company's commercialization partner in China, the Company made a decision to pause shipments to China beginning in February 2025 and has not resumed shipments to date.
diffs.signalNote: The indefinite China Gardasil pause removes a major growth driver and creates ongoing revenue uncertainty.

diffs.headline: Subcutaneous Keytruda Qlex approved in U.S. and EU
diffs.summary: Merck highlighted FDA approval in September 2025 and EC approval in November 2025 for Keytruda Qlex, a subcutaneous fixed combination of pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Keytruda Qlex , which was initially approved by the FDA in September 2025, is approved in the U.S. in solid tumor indications approved for Keytruda . In November 2025, the EC approved a new subcutaneous (SC) route
diffs.signalNote: Subcutaneous Keytruda approval is critical for extending franchise durability ahead of the 2028 patent cliff.

diffs.headline: 2025 restructuring cash outflows expected to be offset by asset sales
diffs.summary: UnitedHealth disclosed that the net 2026 cash flow impact from 2025 restructuring actions is not expected to be material, as operating cash outflows will be offset by investing cash inflows from held-for-sale business dispositions.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The net impact on 2026 cash flows as a result of the restructuring actions taken in 2025 is not expected to be material, with accruals recorded in 2025 resulting in operating cash outflows, offset by investing cash inflows
diffs.signalNote: Portfolio divestitures are funding restructuring costs without straining 2026 free cash flow.

diffs.headline: Profit growth tied to capacity expansion and higher-margin mix shift
diffs.summary: Philip Morris added MD&A language noting that profit growth could be materially adversely impacted if it fails to expand production capacity to meet demand, raise prices, or shift mix toward higher-margin products and geographies.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Our profit growth may be materially adversely impacted if we are unable to introduce new products or enter new markets successfully, to meet the demand for our products with increased production capacity
diffs.signalNote: Supply capacity for smoke-free products and pricing power remain central to sustaining margin expansion.

diffs.headline: $156.2B defense supplement includes $24.4B for Golden Dome missile shield
diffs.summary: RTX disclosed that new federal legislation provides $156.2 billion in supplementary defense obligations through 2029, including $24.4 billion for the Golden Dome for America next-generation missile defense shield.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The Act also provides a supplementary $156.2 billion to the DoW for obligations through 2029, which includes $24.4 billion for the Golden Dome for America project.
diffs.signalNote: Multi-year Golden Dome funding provides substantial backlog visibility for RTX's missile defense and space segments.

diffs.headline: China localization mandates and tariff volatility flagged as risks
diffs.summary: Thermo Fisher added risk disclosure on Chinese regulations requiring local supplier partnerships and government incentives for local procurement, alongside expanded tariff volatility language.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Chinese regulations requiring the use of local suppliers, which compel companies that do business in China to partner with local companies to conduct business and provide incentives to government-backed local customers
diffs.signalNote: China localization rules threaten TMO's direct commercial share in government-backed life sciences procurement.

diffs.headline: Texas Instruments to acquire Silicon Labs for $7.5B in all-cash deal
diffs.summary: Texas Instruments disclosed its February 4, 2026 definitive agreement to acquire Silicon Labs for $231.00 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of approximately $7.5 billion, expected to close in H1 2027.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: As announced on February 4, 2026, we have entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Silicon Labs for $231.00 per share in an all-cash transaction, representing a total enterprise value of approximately $7.5 billion.
diffs.signalNote: The $7.5B all-cash Silicon Labs acquisition expands TXN's embedded wireless portfolio while committing significant balance sheet cash.

diffs.headline: OBBBA tax law and expanded CHIPS ITC to lower 2026+ cash taxes
diffs.summary: TXN disclosed that the July 2025 OBBBA allows immediate expensing of U.S. R&D and eligible capex and increases the CHIPS Act investment tax credit, lowering effective tax rates and cash tax payments from 2026 onward.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The OBBBA provides changes to U.S. federal tax law, including expensing of U.S. research expenditures and eligible capital expenditures, increasing the U.S. CHIPS and Science Act (CHIPS Act) investment tax credit (ITC)
diffs.signalNote: Higher CHIPS ITC and immediate capex expensing materially improve returns on TXN's multi-year U.S. fab buildout.

diffs.headline: Bridge loan commitments raised to $42.2B for WBD streaming/studios deal
diffs.summary: Netflix disclosed that on January 19, 2026, it increased its senior unsecured bridge term loan commitments from $34.0 billion to $42.2 billion to finance its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery's streaming and studios businesses, including HBO.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The Incremental Commitments Agreement increased the existing commitments under the Company's Bridge Facility Commitments from $34 billion to $42.2 billion of senior unsecured bridge term loan commitments
diffs.signalNote: A $42.2B debt-financed acquisition of WBD's studios and HBO fundamentally transforms Netflix's leverage profile and content scale.

diffs.headline: Tariff mitigation and raw material sourcing adjustments highlighted
diffs.summary: Amgen added risk disclosures on evaluating its global supply chains, raw material sourcing, and manufacturing network to minimize the impact of existing and proposed U.S. and foreign tariffs.
diffs.priorExcerpt: As part of our ongoing business continuity efforts, we continue to closely monitor our inventory levels and have taken additional measures to mitigate against raw material supply interruption.
diffs.currentExcerpt: We also continue to assess the potential impacts of existing and proposed tariffs on our raw material and medical device supply chains and implement sourcing
diffs.signalNote: Active supply chain re-routing may add near-term operating friction as Amgen scales manufacturing.

diffs.headline: Caterpillar projects $2.6B tariff impact in 2026, up $800M YoY
diffs.summary: Caterpillar disclosed that based on incremental tariffs in place by January 29, 2026, it expects a ~$2.6 billion tariff impact in 2026 ($800 million higher than 2025), which could be 20% higher without planned mitigating actions.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Based on the incremental tariffs announced in 2025 and in place by January 29, 2026, we expect the impact from tariffs to be around $2.6 billion in 2026, which is $800 million higher than incurred in 2025.
diffs.signalNote: A $2.6B gross tariff headwind puts a spotlight on CAT's pricing power and supply chain mitigation execution in 2026.

diffs.headline: Investing cash outflows rise 23% to $5.72B on higher capex
diffs.summary: Linde reported that net cash used for investing activities increased from $4,644 million in 2024 to $5,721 million in 2025, driven primarily by higher capital expenditures.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Net cash used for investing activities was $4,644 million in 2024 compared to $4,670 million in 2023.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Net cash used for investing activities was $5,721 million in 2025 compared to $4,644 million in 2024. The increase was primarily attributable to higher capital expenditures.
diffs.signalNote: Stepped-up capex reflects Linde's expanding backlog of clean hydrogen and industrial gas on-site projects.

diffs.headline: Chinese rare earth export controls flagged as supply chain risk
diffs.summary: Lam Research added risk language highlighting potential difficulties or delays in obtaining required import or export approvals under Chinese export controls on rare earth elements.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: difficulties or delays in obtaining required import or export approvals (including those that may be required under the Chinese export controls on rare earth elements described above);
diffs.signalNote: Rare earth export restrictions from China could constrain component availability for wafer fab equipment.

diffs.headline: AI IP protection uncertainty and employee tool leakage risks added
diffs.summary: Lam Research disclosed risks around unsettled AI patent/copyright law and potential IP leakage or license breaches from employee use of third-party AI tools.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The intellectual property rights, including patent and copyright rights, associated with artificial intelligence have not been fully addressed by U.S. and foreign courts
diffs.signalNote: Unsettled AI IP rules and internal tool governance add compliance overhead for R&D-heavy semi-cap players.

diffs.headline: Cybersecurity Advisory Committee expanded across business and corporate units
diffs.summary: IBM updated its cybersecurity governance disclosure to specify that its Cybersecurity Advisory Committee now includes SVPs from Software, Consulting, Infrastructure, Legal, Finance, and Marketing/Communications.
diffs.priorExcerpt: The CAC is composed of, among others, SVPs from the major business units, the SVP Sponsor, and the CLO.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The Cybersecurity Advisory Committee ("CAC") is a senior executive committee comprised of SVPs from the business (Software, Consulting, Infrastructure) and corporate functions (Legal, Finance, Marketing/Communications)
diffs.signalNote: Broader cross-functional cyber governance reflects heightened enterprise incident escalation standards.

diffs.headline: Fluid U.S. tariffs and retaliatory measures flagged as margin risk
diffs.summary: Arista Networks added risk disclosures warning that escalating U.S. tariffs and retaliatory trade actions could raise production costs, impair international manufacturing profitability, and strain supplier capacity.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: An increase in trade-related costs associated with these tariff actions may affect our cost of production, impair the profitability of our international production, affect our ability to procure certain items
diffs.signalNote: Tariff volatility could pressure Arista's hardware gross margins alongside large-scale customer pricing discounts.

diffs.headline: Large-scale order pricing discounts cited as gross margin drag
diffs.summary: Arista noted in MD&A that pricing discounts typically required for large-scale orders often reduce gross margins in the periods when those sales occur.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Additionally, the pricing discounts typically required for these large-scale orders often reduce gross margins in the periods when the sales occur.
diffs.signalNote: Hyperscale AI networking wins carry periodic gross margin dilution due to volume discounting.

diffs.headline: DCF fair value assumptions flagged for sensitivity to market shifts
diffs.summary: Disney added MD&A disclosure emphasizing that discounted cash flow fair value models rely on significant judgments around future revenues, margins, terminal growth, and discount rates that could be impacted by market shifts.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Significant judgments and assumptions in the discounted cash flow model used to determine fair value relate to future revenues and certain operating expenses, operating margins, terminal growth rates and discount rates.
diffs.signalNote: Increased sensitivity in DCF assumptions signals potential goodwill or asset impairment watchpoints if linear TV trends soften.

diffs.headline: Biktarvy patent settlements push U.S. generic entry to April 2036
diffs.summary: Gilead disclosed October 2025 patent litigation settlements with Lupin, Cipla, and Laurus Labs, under which no generic Biktarvy entry is expected in the U.S. prior to April 1, 2036, subject to standard acceleration provisions.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.

diffs.priorExcerpt: The traditional electric operating companies are experiencing projected demand that exceeds recent experience, creating the need for new power generating resources
diffs.currentExcerpt: The traditional electric operating companies are experiencing projected demand that significantly exceeds recent experience, creating the need for new power generating resources and transmission facilities.
diffs.signalNote: Accelerating AI data center load underpins multi-year regulated ratebase growth across Southern's Southeast footprint.

diffs.headline: 77% of $2.8B capex directed to technology and digital initiatives
diffs.summary: CVS Health disclosed that gross capital expenditures were ~$2.8 billion in both 2025 and 2024, with 77% in 2025 allocated to technology, digital, and strategic initiatives versus 23% to stores and fulfillment.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: During 2025, approximately 77% of the Company's total capital expenditures were for technology, digital and other strategic initiatives and 23% were for store, fulfillment and support facilities
diffs.signalNote: Heavy tech and digital capex weighting reflects CVS's pivot away from physical retail store expansion.

diffs.headline: Redesigned app with AI personalization and services expansion launched
diffs.summary: Airbnb updated its business and regulatory disclosures to reflect its 2025 app redesign featuring unified search, AI-powered personalization, and expanded services offerings, alongside AI and e-commerce regulatory risks.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Our website and mobile app provide our guests with an engaging way to explore and easily book a wide variety of unique homes and experiences.
diffs.currentExcerpt: In 2025, we launched a redesigned app experience featuring unified search and booking for all offerings, artificial intelligence ("AI")-powered
diffs.signalNote: Expanding beyond stays into services and AI-driven discovery aims to boost booking frequency and take-rate durability.

diffs.headline: Newmont initiates Q3 2025 workforce and office restructuring plan
diffs.summary: Newmont disclosed that at the start of Q3 2025 management committed to a cost-reduction plan involving organizational streamlining, workforce reductions, and office space consolidation, incurring severance and restructuring charges.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: At the beginning of the third quarter of 2025, management committed to a strategic plan designed to reduce operating costs and continue to advance the Company's ongoing commitment to profitability
diffs.signalNote: Streamlining overhead post-Newcrest integration is aimed at protecting free cash flow across commodity cycles.

diffs.headline: Hyperscale data center load growth flags stranded asset risk
diffs.summary: Duke Energy added disclosure warning that hyperscale data centers and large industrial loads create rapid demand fluctuations and grid stability strain. Meeting this load requires heavy generation and transmission capex, exposing Duke to stranded asset risk if service agreements terminate early.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: emerging large loads such as hyperscale data centers and industrial facilities present unique risks due to their high demand, rapid fluctuations, and unpredictable operational profiles
diffs.signalNote: Watch for minimum-demand or take-or-pay contract protections in Duke's upcoming regulatory rate filings.

diffs.headline: Rare earth export controls and tariffs threaten grid capex
diffs.summary: The filing introduces new supply chain risk language around potential export controls on rare earth materials and utility technologies. Management also warns that lower-than-anticipated asset sale proceeds could force alternative funding or delay displacement of planned debt and equity issuances.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: potential export controls on certain rare earth materials and technologies used in electric utility infrastructure, may further constrain supply availability.
diffs.signalNote: Monitor equipment lead times and equity issuance plans if asset disposition proceeds fall short.

diffs.headline: Excess and obsolete inventory reserve assumptions tied to gross margin
diffs.summary: Western Digital added MD&A disclosure detailing that excess and obsolete inventory reserves are released only when underlying units are sold or scrapped. Unfavorable shifts in technology or demand assumptions could require additional write-downs that materially pressure gross margin.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: If in any period we anticipate a change in those assumptions to be less favorable than our previous estimates, additional inventory write-downs may be required and could materially and negatively impact our gross margin.
diffs.signalNote: Track inventory days and gross margin sensitivity to NAND/HDD demand cycles in upcoming quarters.

diffs.headline: AI operational adoption and EU AI Act compliance risks added
diffs.summary: WDC introduced risk factors covering costly generative AI implementation and potential violations of global AI regulations, including the EU Artificial Intelligence Act. Non-compliance or misuse could trigger data protection and intellectual property liabilities.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Governments worldwide are adopting or proposing AI-specific regulations, including the European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act, as well as various proposed frameworks in the U.S., China, and other jurisdictions.
diffs.signalNote: AI governance compliance costs are emerging as a standard operational overhead for hardware and storage peers.

diffs.headline: Retaliatory tariffs and foreign restrictions threaten international sales
diffs.summary: Cloudflare added new risk factor language warning that U.S. tariffs have prompted or could prompt retaliatory taxes, tariffs, or operational restrictions on U.S. tech companies abroad. These measures could directly impair international product sales and customer adoption.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: many of the countries subject to these tariffs have themselves implemented or threatened to implement tariffs, taxes, or other retaliatory measures on U.S. goods or services or U.S. companies
diffs.signalNote: International revenue growth could face headwinds if foreign governments target U.S. cloud providers in trade disputes.

diffs.headline: Federal Acquisition Regulations expand compliance exposure
diffs.summary: MD&A now highlights expanded compliance obligations under the Federal Acquisition Regulations for direct and channel-partner sales to the U.S. government. Non-compliance by Cloudflare or its partners could result in investigations and fines.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Selling our products to the U.S. government, whether directly or through channel partners, also subjects us to certain regulatory and contractual requirements, including expanded compliance obligations under the Federal Acquisition Regulations.
diffs.signalNote: Public-sector momentum brings higher regulatory audit and partner-oversight requirements.

diffs.headline: Gross margin pressured by inventory write-offs and Libtayo amortization
diffs.summary: Regeneron disclosed that 2025 gross margin on net product sales declined versus 2024 due to ongoing manufacturing investments, higher inventory write-offs and reserves, and rising amortization of the Libtayo intangible asset tied to Sanofi royalties.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Gross margin on net product sales decreased in 2025, compared to 2024, partly due to ongoing investments to support our manufacturing operations and higher inventory write-offs and reserves.
diffs.signalNote: Monitor whether manufacturing scale-up and Libtayo royalty amortization continue to compress product gross margins in 2026.

diffs.headline: Chinese biotech competition and 340B ceiling price expansion flagged
diffs.summary: REGN added specific risk language on Chinese state-backed biotechs leveraging low-cost, rapid clinical trials, alongside state-level legislation that could expand federal 340B ceiling price applicability. EYLEA HD and EYLEA also face intensifying VEGF inhibitor and biosimilar competition.
diffs.priorExcerpt: At the state level, legislatures are becoming increasingly aggressive in passing legislation and implementing regulations designed to control pharmaceutical and biological product pricing
diffs.currentExcerpt: measures that could expand the applicability of the ceiling price under the federal government's 340B program
diffs.signalNote: 340B expansion and EYLEA biosimilar pressure remain key variables for U.S. net pricing durability.

diffs.headline: Low-carbon and pipeline projects face permitting and cancellation risks
diffs.summary: Valero added disclosure noting that opposition to both fossil fuel infrastructure and low-carbon projects, including carbon capture and sequestration, is making project approvals more difficult and costly. Such opposition has previously caused project cancellations or restructurings.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: challenges to or opposition of certain fossil fuel and infrastructure projects (including pipelines), as well as certain low-carbon projects (such as carbon sequestration and carbon capture and storage), continue to make the approval and completion of such projects more difficult and costly.
diffs.signalNote: Watch for potential capex delays or write-offs in Valero's low-carbon and pipeline development pipeline.

diffs.headline: Regulatory policy uncertainty and landfill remediation accruals highlighted
diffs.summary: Waste Management updated its regulatory risk factor to note that the current administration's trade and deregulatory shifts remain uncertain due to ongoing litigation and agency reviews. In MD&A, WM also emphasized that landfill closure and environmental remediation expenditures could accelerate beyond current accruals.
diffs.priorExcerpt: be in favor of reducing regulation, including environmental regulation. We do not know what impact the change in U.S. presidential administration will have on specific regulatory policies
diffs.currentExcerpt: The current administration has called for, and undertaken, substantial changes to areas of foreign trade policy and is generally in favor of reducing regulation, including environmental regulation. The impact and timing of these shifts in regulatory policy impacting our industry and our Company remain uncertain
diffs.signalNote: Track EPA litigation outcomes and landfill closure accrual adjustments for potential cash flow timing impacts.

diffs.headline: OBBBA tax law shifts ICE provision from current to deferred taxes
diffs.summary: Intercontinental Exchange disclosed that the July 2025 enactment of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) did not materially alter its 2025 effective tax rate. However, immediate expensing provisions shifted the tax provision mix toward lower current income tax expense and higher deferred tax expense.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The composition of the income tax provision, however, reflects a decrease in current income tax expenses, offset by an increase in deferred income tax expenses, primarily due to immediate expensing
diffs.signalNote: Lower current cash taxes from immediate expensing provide a near-term free cash flow tailwind.

diffs.headline: PSX recycles $3.5B in asset sales into WRB buyout and 2026 capex
diffs.summary: Phillips 66 disclosed $3.5 billion in 2025 asset disposition proceeds, including $1.7 billion from selling 65% of its Germany and Austria retail business, funding a $2.2 billion Midstream acquisition and $1.3 billion for the remaining 50% of WRB Refining. Management budgeted $2.4 billion for 2026 capex, including $1.3 billion for growth.
diffs.priorExcerpt: In 2024, we funded capital expenditures and investments of $1.9 billion and completed acquisitions of $0.6 billion through disciplined capital allocation and $1.1 billion in proceeds from asset dispositions.
diffs.currentExcerpt: We budgeted $2.4 billion for 2026 capital expenditures and investments, exclusive of acquisitions and our share of capital spending by equity affiliates. This includes $1.3 billion of growth capital, primarily in our Midstream segment.
diffs.signalNote: Portfolio rotation into Midstream and full WRB ownership sharpens PSX's integrated U.S. refining and NGL footprint.

diffs.headline: Refining results offset by $948M before-tax equity impairment
diffs.summary: PSX reported that 2025 Refining segment results rose $91 million on improved market crack spreads and higher volumes, but were partially offset by higher RIN costs, weaker product differentials, and a $948 million before-tax impairment.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Results from the Refining segment decreased $2,636 million in 2023, compared with 2022. The decrease was primarily due to lower realized margins, partially offset by lower utility costs.
diffs.currentExcerpt: the increase in 2025 was partially offset by a before-tax impairment of $948 million related to our equity met
diffs.signalNote: Assess whether the $948M equity impairment clears remaining book-value overhang in non-core refining assets.

diffs.headline: PFAS exit and Solventum spin create margin dis-synergies and tariff drag
diffs.summary: 3M disclosed that 2025 operating margins benefited from productivity and lower restructuring, but faced headwinds from tariff impacts, growth investments, and cost dis-synergies from exiting PFAS manufacturing and spinning off Solventum. Third-party PFAS-free component sourcing remains under evaluation.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: margins YoY were impacted by cost dis-synergies (from the exit of PFAS manufacturing and 2024 spin of Solventum); by transition service agreement reimbursement from Solventum, which began in the second quarter of 2024
diffs.signalNote: Track the pace of stranded-cost elimination as Solventum transition service reimbursements taper off.

diffs.headline: Aerospace business jet output remains gated by supply chain
diffs.summary: General Dynamics noted in MD&A that Aerospace continues to experience strong demand for business jets, but new aircraft production remains dependent on supply chain execution despite recent performance improvements. Investing cash outflows also rose to $1.3 billion in 2025 from $953 million in 2024.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: In our principal commercial market, Aerospace is experiencing strong demand for business jets. Our ability to produce new aircraft is dependent on our supply chain, and while performance has improved
diffs.signalNote: Gulfstream delivery cadence and margin conversion remain tied to supplier reliability.

diffs.headline: Cloud-hosted security transition adds uncertainty to billings and margins
diffs.summary: Fortinet expanded its risk factor on cloud-based and hosted security solutions to highlight increased demand alongside uncertainty in transitioning its business model toward hosted services. Management warns billings, revenue, free cash flow, and operating margins could slow if renewal rates or pricing soften.
diffs.priorExcerpt: the impact of cloud-based and hosted security solutions on our billings, revenue, operating margins and free cash flow;
diffs.currentExcerpt: the impact of cloud-based and hosted security solutions, including increased demand for such services and uncertainty associated with transition to providing such services, on our billings, revenue, operating margins and free cash flow;
diffs.signalNote: Watch cloud-delivered billings mix and gross margin trajectory as Fortinet balances hardware refresh with SaaS.

diffs.headline: FortiAI dual-layered agentic AI security framework introduced
diffs.summary: MD&A now details FortiAI, a dual-layered framework spanning AI for Security (FortiAI-Assist for NOC/SOC teams) and Security for AI (FortiAI-Protect and FortiAI-SecureAI for GenAI governance and zero-day threats).
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: FortiAI - FortiAI provides a dual-layered defense across the Fortinet Security Fabric through the AI for Security and Security for AI framework.
diffs.signalNote: Monitor customer attach rates for FortiAI modules as an indicator of platform upsell.

diffs.headline: CSX updates CISO leadership and shifts SOC support to MSSP
diffs.summary: CSX updated its cybersecurity governance disclosure, noting that the program is now led by the Assistant VP of Cloud Infrastructure Platforms and CISO, supported by internal staff and a Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) rather than the prior Deputy Chief SOC structure.
diffs.priorExcerpt: The cybersecurity program and related risks at CSX are managed by the VP Technology and CISO . The Company's CISO is a Certified Information Systems Auditor with over 30 years of industry experience
diffs.currentExcerpt: The cybersecurity program and related risks at CSX are managed by the Assistant Vice President of Cloud Infrastructure Platforms and CISO . The Company's CISO has over 29 years of industry experience
diffs.signalNote: Routine governance update reflecting outsourced SOC augmentation.

diffs.headline: Amazon revenue share drops to 10.6% as UPS cuts network assets
diffs.summary: UPS updated its Amazon concentration disclosure, noting Amazon accounted for 10.6% of 2025 consolidated revenue (down from 11.8% in 2024) under its planned volume reduction strategy. To avoid stranded costs, UPS is actively reducing facilities, vehicles, aircraft, and workforce.
diffs.priorExcerpt: For the year ended December 31, 2024, one customer, Amazon.com, Inc. and its affiliates, accounted for 11.8% of our consolidated revenues. In the first quarter of 2025, we entered into an agreement in principle
diffs.currentExcerpt: Our strategy includes planned volume declines from our largest customer, Amazon.com, Inc. For 2025, this customer and its affiliates accounted for 10.6% of our consolidated revenues.
diffs.signalNote: Execution on network rightsizing is critical to prevent stranded-cost margin drag as Amazon volume steps down.

diffs.headline: Tariffs and de minimis exclusions pressure China-U.S. lane margins
diffs.summary: UPS disclosed in MD&A that 2025 tariffs and de minimis exclusions shifted global trade lane volumes, specifically reducing China-to-U.S. volume and pressuring International Package segment margins.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Global trade policy changes during 2025, including pending and enacted tariffs and de minimis exclusions, resulted in shifting trade lane volumes, particularly reducing volumes on our China to U.S. lane, pressuring our International Package segment margins
diffs.signalNote: International Package margin recovery depends on trade lane rebalancing away from China-U.S. e-commerce.

diffs.headline: Comcast completes tax-free Versant spin-off on January 2, 2026
diffs.summary: Comcast disclosed the completion of the Versant separation via a tax-free spin-off of 100% of Versant common stock to Comcast shareholders on January 2, 2026. Versant's results were still included in Comcast's Media segment for all 2025 periods presented.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The Separation was structured to qualify as a tax-free spin-off for U.S. federal income tax purposes and achieved through the transfer of assets and liabilities comprising the Versant business to Versant and its subsidiaries, followed by the distribution on January 2, 2026
diffs.signalNote: Expect cleaner Media segment comparability and standalone capital allocation clarity beginning in Q1 2026.

diffs.headline: Cintas secures $2.85B bridge facility for pending M&A transaction
diffs.summary: Cintas disclosed a March 10, 2026 commitment letter for a $2.85 billion 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility to support its pending acquisition. In Item 1A, Cintas warned that failure to close would forfeit expected synergies while leaving the company with significant transaction fees and potential stock price pressure.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: we also entered into a commitment letter on March 10, 2026 with certain debt commitment parties, who have committed to provide a 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility in an aggregate principal amount of $2.85 billion (the Bridge Facility)
diffs.signalNote: Monitor regulatory closing milestones and permanent debt take-out terms for the $2.85B bridge facility.

diffs.headline: AI regulations drive more onerous customer contract obligations
diffs.summary: Adobe disclosed that evolving AI and data laws have already resulted in more onerous contractual obligations and business practice changes, and may require further adjustments that affect customer relationship duration and revenue.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The laws, regulations and codes above may impact our innovation and business drivers in developing new and emerging technologies (for example, AI and machine learning) and may impact demand for our solutions and has resulted in more onerous obligations in our contracts
diffs.signalNote: Watch for enterprise AI indemnification and compliance clauses lengthening sales cycles.

diffs.headline: MSI expands AI risk focus to IP infringement and flawed outputs
diffs.summary: Motorola Solutions shifted its AI risk factor from social/ethical controversy to operational and legal exposure from flawed data, inaccurate or biased AI recommendations, and third-party IP infringement. Management also highlighted AI-powered capabilities and cybersecurity subscriptions across all three core technologies.
diffs.priorExcerpt: As we increasingly leverage AI, including generative AI, in our offerings, we may enable or offer products and services that draw controversy due to their actual or perceived impact on social and ethical issues
diffs.currentExcerpt: if we use AI that is based on data, algorithms, or other inputs that are flawed or insufficient, or if the AI assists in producing content, analyses or recommendations that are or are alleged to be deficient, inaccurate, violative of third-party intellectual property, or biased
diffs.signalNote: Public-safety AI adoption brings heightened accuracy and IP liability standards.

diffs.headline: State ingredient bans and labeling laws add reformulation risk
diffs.summary: Monster Beverage added disclosure on state-level food ingredient bans, citing West Virginia's 2025 ban on seven color additives and two preservatives (currently stayed by preliminary injunction) and new Texas labeling legislation.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: West Virginia enacted legislation in 2025 that includes a ban on seven color additives and two preservatives products marketed to the general public; however, such portion of the law was challenged, and the court has granted a preliminary injunction
diffs.signalNote: Track state-level ingredient litigation as fragmented labeling rules could increase packaging and reformulation costs.

diffs.headline: CMS Marketplace Integrity rule and litigation create ACA uncertainty
diffs.summary: Elevance Health disclosed in MD&A that CMS finalized the Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Regulation in June 2025, modifying 2027 public exchange open enrollment and PTC eligibility, though a federal court delayed several provisions in September 2025 pending litigation.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: in June 2025, CMS finalized the Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Regulation, which modifies the Public exchange open enrollment period beginning in plan year 2027 and eligibility for PTCs, among other requirements. In September 2025, a federal court delayed the effective dates
diffs.signalNote: ACA exchange enrollment and subsidy eligibility for 2027 hinge on the outcome of federal court challenges.

diffs.headline: 2025 U.S. and retaliatory tariffs drive commodity and supply chain risk
diffs.summary: Trane Technologies added MD&A disclosure warning that 2025 U.S. tariffs and retaliatory foreign tariffs create dynamic supply chain challenges, commodity cost volatility, and economic uncertainty, though management relies on its in-region-for-region strategy to navigate.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: uncertainties resulting from the tariffs announced and implemented by the United States in 2025, as well as the tariffs imposed by other countries in response. These global trade policy changes continue to be dynamic and, as a result, we may experience supply chain challenges, commodity cost volatility
diffs.signalNote: Monitor HVAC gross margin resilience against copper, steel, and cross-border component tariff pressure.

diffs.headline: Product gross margin ticks up to 72% despite new feature scaling
diffs.summary: Snowflake reported product gross margin improved to 72% in FY2026 from 71% in FY2025, driven by lower personnel and restructuring costs as a percentage of product revenue, partially offset by newly launched features not yet at scale.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Our product gross margin was 72% for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, compared to 71% for the prior fiscal year. This slight improvement is primarily due to the decrease in personnel-related costs
diffs.signalNote: Watch whether AI and new product feature adoption scales fast enough to sustain gross margin expansion.

diffs.headline: External platform integrations and AI offerings heighten cyber risk
diffs.summary: Snowflake expanded its cybersecurity risk factor to warn that operating in and integrating with external environments outside its platform, alongside expanding AI offerings and acquisitions, increases data incident exposure.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Our insurance coverage may not be adequate for liability arising from data security breaches involving us or our customers or other third parties
diffs.currentExcerpt: the risk of cybersecurity and data incidents will increase as we continue to expand our product offerings and geographic footprint, grow our customer and partner base, expand our AI Technology offerings, acquire operating companies, begin to operate in and integrate with environments outside of our platform
diffs.signalNote: Third-party environment integrations widen Snowflake's security perimeter as it pushes into external data.

diffs.headline: Ultra-processed food addiction lawsuit cited in litigation risk
diffs.summary: Mondelez added specific disclosure citing the December 2024 Bryce Martinez v. Kraft Heinz Co. et al. personal injury lawsuit alleging certain food products are addictive and cause health problems. Management intends to vigorously defend the suit.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: a purported personal injury lawsuit filed in December 2024 against a number of food companies, including us ( Bryce Martinez vs. Kraft Heinz Co. Inc. et al. ), alleged that certain food products we and other companies make are addictive and cause health problems.
diffs.signalNote: Monitor early motions in ultra-processed food litigation for potential industry-wide legal overhang.

diffs.headline: CEG highlights 835 MW Crane Clean Energy restart and data center load
diffs.summary: Constellation Energy updated its AI and data center demand disclosure, adding Meta alongside Microsoft, Google, and Amazon as hyperscaler drivers, and specifying that the Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart (Crane Clean Energy Center) will deliver approximately 835 MW of emissions-free power.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Significant planned investments from hyperscalers such as Microsoft, Google, and Amazon in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and infrastructure are further contributing to unprecedented demand
diffs.currentExcerpt: The site, once operational, will have approximately 835 MWs of emissions-free energy
diffs.signalNote: Crane Clean Energy Center's 835 MW restart anchors CEG's long-term nuclear PPA pricing power.

diffs.headline: Howmet agrees to $1.8B CAM acquisition from Stanley Black & Decker
diffs.summary: Howmet Aerospace disclosed a December 22, 2025 agreement to acquire CAM from Stanley Black & Decker for approximately $1.8 billion in cash, expected to close in H1 2026, alongside the February 6, 2026 acquisition of Brunner Manufacturing.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: On December 22, 2025, Howmet Aerospace entered into a transaction with Stanley Black & Decker, pursuant to which the Company has agreed to purchase CAM, for a cash purchase price of approximately $1.8 billion
diffs.signalNote: Watch for H1 2026 closing, leverage impact, and fastener/aerospace synergy targets from the $1.8B CAM deal.

diffs.headline: 2025 U.S. and retaliatory tariffs create ongoing trade uncertainty
diffs.summary: Ecolab updated its trade risk factor to reflect that new U.S. tariffs were imposed across a broad range of countries and materials in 2025, prompting retaliatory tariffs and creating ongoing policy uncertainty. Reported diluted EPS dipped 1% to $7.28 due to One Ecolab charges, while adjusted diluted EPS rose 13% to $7.53.
diffs.priorExcerpt: In February 2025, the U.S. proposed a 25
diffs.currentExcerpt: During 2025, new tariffs were imposed in the U.S. for imports from a broad range of countries and materials. Several countries also implemented or proposed retaliatory tariffs on imports from the U.S.
diffs.signalNote: Value pricing and One Ecolab productivity offset tariff headwinds in 2025; watch 2026 input cost pass-through.

diffs.headline: EU AI Act and cross-border data localization risks added
diffs.summary: Moody's introduced new risk factor disclosures covering compliance costs and potential penalties under the EU AI Act, alongside restrictive government actions on cross-border data transfers, data localization, and tariffs.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The EU AI Act has introduced a risk-based framework for regulating AI systems which applies different obligations to various participants in the AI supply chain. Compliance with the regulation, in its current form, could increase the Company's costs
diffs.signalNote: Monitor compliance overhead in Moody's Analytics as EU AI Act implementation rules finalize.

diffs.headline: Hilton flags cash payment exposure if hotel owners default on debt
diffs.summary: Hilton added disclosure warning that third-party hotel owners face higher refinancing difficulty in the current interest rate environment. Lender defaults or repossessions have required, and may in the future require, Hilton to make cash payments or incur contract termination losses.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: If our third-party hotel owners are unable to repay or refinance maturing indebtedness on favorable terms or at all, which could be more difficult in the current interest rate environment, their lenders could declare a default
diffs.signalNote: Watch franchisee refinancing health and any key-money or guarantee outlays in higher-for-longer rate markets.

diffs.headline: CFO Naftali Holtz adds supply chain oversight to remit
diffs.summary: Royal Caribbean updated its executive officer disclosure to reflect that CFO Naftali Holtz's responsibilities now explicitly include supply chain oversight alongside financial planning, risk management, and treasury.
diffs.priorExcerpt: Prior to his role as Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Holtz served as Senior Vice President of Finance, responsible for financial planning and analysis, risk management and treasury.
diffs.currentExcerpt: In his role as Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Holtz is responsible for overseeing the Company's financial planning and analysis, supply chain, risk management, corporate strategy and development
diffs.signalNote: Centralizing supply chain under the CFO underscores focus on shipbuilding and operating cost discipline.

diffs.headline: Data center capex cycles and power bottlenecks threaten backlog
diffs.summary: Johnson Controls added a dedicated risk factor warning that data center construction is tied to concentrated tech-sector capex cycles and logistical bottlenecks such as power availability and permitting. A spending pullback by a small number of large tech customers could disproportionately hit JCI's order pipeline and backlog.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: a reduction in spending by a small number of large technology customers due to business, financial, political or logistical (i.e., electrical power availability, permitting, zoning and regulatory approvals) constraints could disproportionately affect our order pipeline and backlog.
diffs.signalNote: Monitor hyperscaler capex guidance and grid interconnection delays for early signs of HVAC order deceleration.

diffs.headline: China weakness triggers interim impairment review on Filorga skin health
diffs.summary: Colgate-Palmolive disclosed in MD&A that weaker-than-expected performance in China and lower category growth led it to lower its Q4 2025 outlook for the skin health reporting unit (primarily Filorga), triggering an interim impairment review of goodwill and long-lived assets.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: Given lower than expected category growth rates and weaker than expected performance, particularly in China, in the fourth quarter of 2025 the Company lowered its outlook for the skin health reporting unit, primarily Filorga.
diffs.signalNote: Watch for any goodwill or trademark write-down disclosures and China skin-health stabilization.

diffs.headline: Williams signs 1.9 GW of 12.5-year data center power agreements
diffs.summary: Williams disclosed in MD&A that it is investing in onsite natural gas and power generation projects in Ohio and Utah totaling 1.9 GW of capacity, backed by up to 12.5-year primarily fixed-price agreements with a large investment-grade customer.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: The projects, located in Ohio and Utah, represent a combined 1.9 gigawatts of total capacity and are backed by up to 12.5 year, primarily fixed-price agreements, with an option for the customer to extend
diffs.signalNote: Long-term fixed-price power contracts diversify WMB's midstream cash flows into behind-the-meter data center demand.

diffs.headline: EOG closes $5.7B Encino acquisition adding 675,000 Utica net acres
diffs.summary: EOG Resources disclosed the August 1, 2025 completion of its $5.7 billion acquisition of Encino Acquisition Partners (inclusive of net debt), adding 675,000 core net acres in the Utica play and contributing to consolidated results from August onward.
diffs.priorExcerpt: No equivalent disclosure language appeared in the prior 10-K.
diffs.currentExcerpt: On August 1, 2025, EOG completed its acquisition of Encino Acquisition Partners, LLC (Encino) for $5.7 billion, inclusive of Encino's net debt. The assets of Encino include 675,000 core net acres in the Utica play.

diffs.summary: Maplebear (Instacart) added risk disclosures noting that macroeconomic caution has caused brands to slow or reduce advertising campaigns on its platform. It also added a standalone AI risk factor covering competitive and legal liabilities.

diffs.headline: Weyerhaeuser Establishes $1.75B Commercial Paper Program and Swaps $800M Loan
diffs.summary: In November 2025, Weyerhaeuser established a $1.75 billion commercial paper program for short-term liquidity. Earlier in Q3 2025, it entered interest rate swaps to convert its new $800 million variable-rate term loan into fixed-rate payments.

diffs.currentExcerpt: In November 2025, we established a commercial paper program under which we may issue short-term, unsecured commercial paper notes... in an aggregate amount not to exceed $1.75 billion outstanding at any time.
diffs.signalNote: New $1.75B commercial paper capacity and $800M term loan hedging enhance liquidity and rate certainty.

diffs.headline: Equitable Holdings Flags AllianceBernstein Conflict and Class Action Risks
diffs.summary: Equitable Holdings added risk disclosures highlighting that AllianceBernstein (AB) must increasingly manage actual and potential conflicts of interest to avoid client attrition or enforcement. It also noted rising frequency of large damage awards in financial services class actions.

diffs.headline: Glaukos Adds AI/ML Regulatory Risk and Healthcare Penalty Disclosures
diffs.summary: Glaukos added a risk factor covering legal, regulatory, and reputational risks from implementing AI and machine learning technologies, alongside detailed disclosures on potential Medicare/Medicaid exclusion and civil or criminal penalties for healthcare law violations.

diffs.headline: Logitech Hit by AI Data Center Demand Driving Memory Chip Price Increases
diffs.summary: Logitech disclosed in MD&A that AI and data center buildouts have driven up prices for memory chips and other components, while some suppliers transitioned capacity away from components used in its Video Collaboration products.

diffs.headline: Logitech Details OECD Pillar Two 15% Minimum Tax Compliance in Switzerland

diffs.headline: Lattice Semiconductor Details 50%-100% China Tariffs and Deemed Export Risks
diffs.summary: Lattice expanded its trade risk factor to cite 50% tariffs on certain Chinese semiconductor items in early 2025, a late-2025 USTR Section 301 finding, and deemed export rules covering remote R&D and source code access.

diffs.headline: Rivian Secures Section 232 Tariff Offset License Through April 2026
diffs.summary: Rivian disclosed that while the U.S. imposed a 25% Section 232 tariff on imported auto parts in May 2025, Rivian received a license in October 2025 to apply tariff offset credits (3.75% of U.S. vehicle MSRP) through April 30, 2026.

diffs.currentExcerpt: Effective May 3, 2025, the United States government adjusted tariffs on imported automobile parts under Section 232... imposing a 25% tariff on many parts but allowing for tariff offset credits...
diffs.signalNote: Tariff offset credits mitigate near-term 25% parts duties, but renewal beyond April 2026 is critical ahead of R2 ramp.

diffs.summary: Rivian added explicit risk language that announcing new EV models such as R2 could hurt near-term revenues if customers delay purchases, alongside supply chain vulnerability for heavy rare earth magnet materials.
